audit.overview: The review covered the three files in scope at the commit above. It found one Critical, one Medium and one Low finding. The Critical finding lets any depositor drain the ether of the others, so fix it before the vault is deployed.

issues.name: withdraw() pays the caller before it lowers the caller's balance
issues.cause: withdraw() sends ether to the caller on line 90 and lowers balances[msg.sender] only on line 92. The caller's receive function runs between the two statements, while the vault still records the old balance.
issues.consequence: A contract that calls withdraw() again from its receive function passes the balance check on every nested call and is paid each time. Any depositor can drain the ether of all other depositors in one transaction.
issues.remediation: Lower balances[msg.sender] before the external call, and add a reentrancy guard to withdraw().

proofs.name: test/poc/F-01-reenter-withdraw.t.sol

issues.name: latestPrice() returns an answer of any age
issues.cause: latestPrice() reads updatedAt on line 42 and never compares it with block.timestamp, so it returns an answer of any age as the current price.
issues.consequence: While the source is delayed, the vault opens and liquidates loans at an old price. The loss on each loan is bounded by the price move during the delay.
issues.remediation: Revert when block.timestamp - updatedAt is greater than a maximum age fixed at deployment.

proofs.name: test/poc/F-02-stale-price.t.sol

issues.name: setRate() changes the rate without an event
issues.cause: setRate() writes rateBps on line 64 and emits no event, so a rate change leaves no log entry.
